title: India meet Pakistan in Asian Games cricket final as hockey, archery chase Olympic quotas
excerpt: Saturday's penultimate day in Aichi-Nagoya brings the men's T20 cricket gold-medal clash against Pakistan at 10:00 AM IST, the men's hockey final against Malaysia at 3:30 PM IST, and recurve archery medal rounds carrying LA 2028 quota places.
body:
• India faces Pakistan in the men's T20 cricket final at 10:00 AM IST on Saturday, October 3, at Kōrogi Sports Park, defending the Asian Games gold won at Hangzhou 2022.
  • The men's hockey team plays Malaysia at 3:30 PM IST for gold and a direct berth at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, hours after the women's team sealed theirs.
  • Recurve archery's individual medal rounds carry LA 2028 quota places, with Kumkum Mohod, Dhiraj Bommadevara and Neeraj Chauhan all in quarterfinal action.
  • India sits fifth in the medal tally with 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze after a medal rush on October 2 headlined by boxing, wrestling and a historic women's hockey triumph.

The penultimate day of the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya is India's biggest of the Games. On Saturday, October 3, two gold-medal team finals — cricket against Pakistan at 10:00 AM IST and men's hockey against Malaysia at 3:30 PM IST — bookend a day packed with Olympic qualification chances in archery, wrestling medal bouts and golf's final rounds.

The headline acts: cricket and hockey finals

At 10:00 AM IST, India defends its men's T20 cricket gold against Pakistan at Kōrogi Sports Park. India reached the final by beating Sri Lanka in Thursday's semifinal and remains the tournament's standard-bearer, having won gold at the Hangzhou Games in 2023, when the final was washed out and the title went to India on higher seeding. The women's team has already delivered, beating Sri Lanka in the final on September 22 to retain its title.

The afternoon brings the men's hockey final at 3:30 PM IST, where Harmanpreet Singh's side faces Malaysia. India is the defending champion and entered Aichi-Nagoya as the outright favourite after unbeaten campaigns at the 2024 Asian Champions Trophy and the 2025 Asia Cup, though the squad has faced scrutiny after an eighth-place finish at the recent World Cup and a difficult FIH Pro League run under coach Craig Fulton.

The hockey final follows Friday's landmark women's final, when India beat defending champions and Olympic silver medallists China 1-0 in Kakamigahara. Lalremsiami scored in the 10th minute of her 200th international appearance, ending a 44-year wait stretching back to 1982 and booking India's women a direct ticket to Los Angeles 2028.

Olympic quotas up for grabs

Saturday's hockey final carries more than a medal. Under the International Hockey Federation's LA 2028 qualification pathway, the winners of both the men's and women's tournaments qualify directly for the Olympics, bypassing the high-risk FIH Olympic Qualification Tournaments entirely. The teams finishing in the top six outside the champion will feed into those qualifiers instead. India's men, who missed a direct route through recent cycles, can lock in a two-year runway to the Games with a win over Malaysia.

Archery offers India's second qualification route. The finalists of the men's and women's individual recurve events earn Olympic quota places — which go to the National Olympic Committee, not the individual athlete — alongside the winners of the mixed-team recurve and compound events. Kumkum Mohod faces South Korea's Kang Chaeyoung in the women's quarterfinal at 5:30 AM IST, with semifinals at 6:30 AM and medal matches at 7:05 AM. Dhiraj Bommadevara takes on Amirkhon Sadikov in the men's quarterfinal at 9:30 AM, Neeraj Chauhan faces Lam Dorji at 10:15 AM, and the men's medal matches close the archery programme at 11:05 AM.

The wider schedule

The day opens on the golf course, with the women's final round at 2:40 AM IST and the men's at 4:45 AM IST. Pranavi Urs holds the sole lead in the women's individual event after the third round, with Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar also in contention; Veer Ahlawat and Yuvraj Sandhu carry India's hopes in the men's event.

Wrestling's medal bouts begin at 2:30 PM IST across five weight classes, with Sagar Jaglan (74kg), Deepak Punia (97kg), Aman Sehrawat (57kg), Manisha (57kg) and Antim Panghal (53kg) all opening in the round of 16 from the morning. Taekwondo sees Kashish Malik and Jyoti Yadav in the women's 57kg and +67kg draws, while the women's rugby sevens side contests 5th-8th place against Singapore and the men's volleyball team faces Thailand in a classification match.

Diaspora angle

An India-Pakistan final remains the single biggest draw for the Indian diaspora in sport — the Gulf, Britain and North America will be watching at dawn local time — and a Saturday double of cricket and hockey finals gives overseas fans a rare shared day of reckoning with the home audience.

What's next

The Games close on October 4 with the closing ceremony in Nagoya, after which India's final tally — currently 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze for fifth place — will be set. Beyond the medal count, October 3 decides how early India's hockey and archery programmes can start planning for Los Angeles.

Live coverage of the day's events is on the Sony Sports Network in India, with streaming on Sony LIV and select events free-to-air on DD Sports.
